name: row
title: Row
description: The shell four specimens draw the same way: 4d's settings row and its Recent row, 4e's failed submit and 4f's code row, all the surface fill with a 3px edge at radius 14, a label that gives way and something at the end that does not. It owns the box and the truncation and nothing else. What sits at the end arrives as `actions`, because the four specimens put a toggle, a retry control and a field there, and a component that tried to be all three would be a worse version of each; it draws no chevron of its own. Two presentations: `settings` is a label and a control, `history` adds the result disc at the front and the delta at the end. A settled row carries `data-gs-state="correct"` or `"wrong"`, the same attribute the rest of the library uses, and the disc says which in a shape and a word as well as a colour. A row the host gives `onSelect` is a real button, so the keyboard works without any key handling; one without is a line of text and not a widget. Performs nothing: it does not navigate, settle a result or know what a delta means.
docs: Pass `label` for the name and `value` for the reading at the end; `value` is a node, so a `stat` can go there. Pass `state` on a settled history row and `actions` for the control at the end, which is where specimen 4d puts a `toggle`. Pass `onSelect` to make the whole row a button. The label is the part that truncates: a player recognises a cut name, and half a number is a wrong number.
